bank.q: Which statement about a class is true?
options: It uses memory for every field when declared
It is a blueprint; memory for fields is used when objects are created
It can only have one object
bank.why: Objects, not classes, hold field values.

bank.q: What does the default constructor look like?
options: It has no parameters and is supplied only if you write no constructor

bank.q: Which keyword refers to the current object?
Fields declared private can be accessed directly from?

bank.why: The reference points to no object.

bank.q: Book a = new Book("X"); Book b = a; b.setTitle("Y"); a.getTitle() is?

options: Book a = new Book(); Book b = a;
Book a = new Book(); Book b = new Book();

bank.q: A static field is shared by?
Distinguish between a class and an object.
bank.model: A class is a blueprint defining fields and methods; an object is a real instance created with new, with its own copy of the fields.

bank.q: What is encapsulation and why is it useful?
bank.model: Hiding fields as private and exposing them through public getters/setters. It protects data, allows validation and lets the class change internally without breaking other code.

bank.q: List the rules for a constructor.
bank.model: Same name as the class; no return type; runs automatically with new; may be overloaded; a default no-argument constructor is supplied only when none is written.

bank.title: Mini project: Library
bank.brief: Write Book (private title, author, price, constructor, getters, toString) and Library with an ArrayList<Book>, addBook, printAll and cheapest() returning the lowest-priced book. In main add 4 books and print the cheapest.
